chapter: Teens with the Salt City Six
title: Sitting in with Vincent Lopez and New York nights
summary: At 14 he sits in on a radio contest at the Taft with Vincent Lopez and is taken to Nick's and the Hickory House to hear Marian McPartland.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well as I said, well okay, between my junior and senior year of high school of course I discovered the joys of physical relationships with women along that period of time. And my girlfriend at the time happened to be the prettiest girl in the school. But I had played, at the age of 15, now I had gotten mononucleosis and had to stay home for two weeks. Mono is a blood — they call it “kissing disease” actually. So anyway, as soon as I got released from that I’m going back to school and Arnie Koch from — they’re reforming the Salt City Six up on Memory Lane up in Syracuse. Jack Maheu, Will Alger, trumpet player Paul Squire, my father on piano — because I had sat in with the Salt City Six prior

to that, when I was 14. But let me preface that by saying that because my eyes were bad at that time we used to go to New York. And we’d go to the Taft Hotel when Vincent Lopez’s band was playing. Because my father — we would stay at the Taft and they used to have a thing called “Shake the Maracas” contest, which was a radio show. And they had me sit in on drums at 14. I’ve got photos of it. And man I was more nervous than a prostitute in church. Or you could say a whore in church. But you can edit that too. So anyway, I sat in. So every time we went there I sat in with them. Then he would take me down to Nick’s to hear either Billy Maxted’s band or whatever band was in Nick’s. And then we’d end the evening — we’d go to Birdland of course, but we’ll get to that a little later — and the Hickory House went to four in the morning so I’d go and hear Marian McPartland’s trio.
